description: Every stable code a surface may branch on. A code is what crosses a boundary; the sentence a reader sees is rendered from it at the last moment, in their language. This file exists because the codes were bare literals repeated across PowerShell, Go and JavaScript with nothing naming them: a code added on one side and forgotten on another stops being recognized, and the surface that missed it reports the state as unknown rather than as an error anyone chases.
rules: A code is lower-case, underscore-separated, and never contains a word a translator would touch.
Every runtime listed under consumedBy must carry the literal. That is the drift this file is checked for: one side learning a code and another not.
rendersAs names the catalog key a reader-facing surface shows for the code. A code with no key is machine-only and says so.
Adding a value to an enumeration is adding a code. It goes here, or some consumer will silently treat it as unknown.
Every entry has one owner, schema version and lifecycle. Deprecation names a replacement and removal release/date; removal moves the wireCode to retiredCodes, and a retired code is never reused.

codes.means: The runner is parked at a step boundary and will not continue until an operator resumes it. The guest stays up and keeps printing, which is why this is a distinct state rather than an absence of progress.
The host's git credential can read the repository it is configured with.
The repository answered and refused. A credential problem, not a network one, and no retry fixes it.
The host was given no repository to read. Distinct from denied: there is nothing to grant access to.
Nothing has asked yet. An absence of evidence, which a surface must not render as a failure.
The service could not reach the authority needed to validate the supplied lab token. This is an availability condition, not a rejected credential.
The service has no configured authority with which to validate a credential, so state-changing operations remain disabled.
A cycle entry began. Carries index, total, name and kind, so a consumer can build a transcript outline without reading the rendered rule.
A cycle entry finished, with its outcome as a lower-case token rather than the word the transcript prints.

Host-update verdict and reason: the running cycle outlasted drainSeconds; the host is untouched and the gate is open again. Action retry_or_drain_now.
Host-update verdict: the resident could not be identified or stopped; the gate is open and nothing was started. Action stop_runner_by_hand.
Host-update state that is not terminal: the runner is to be started and is not running, and the host controller tries again on a backoff until it starts or an operator releases the update.
Host-update verdict: an operator released the update on the host with Invoke-HostUpdate.ps1 -Release; debt lists what was still armed.
Host-update verdict: a new host update took over this one while it was recovering, with its obligations and runner plan.
Host-update verdict: the scope did not complete; restore started the runner on the checkout as it is, or left it stopped as the operator had it. The reason says why.
Host-update verdict: every phase passed and no runner was started, because an operator had stopped it before the update. Action start_runner.
Host-update verdict: current code and the runner running, with at least one remark. Action read_remarks.
Host-update verdict: current code and the runner running, with no remark.
Host-update operator action: end the one-shot run that holds the host, then press again.
Host-update operator action: release the diagnostic hold that keeps a VM for diagnosis, then press again.
Host-update operator action: install the runner's sudo rule with an interactive runner start, then press again.
Host-update operator action after drain_timeout: press again, or run Invoke-HostUpdate.ps1 -Drain now on the host.
Host-update operator action after stop_failed: stop the runner at the host, then press again.
Host-update operator action: the checkout could not be updated or the runner did not start from it; repair the checkout at the host.
Host-update operator action: a condition only a person at the host can change (lock filesystem, home directory, startup config gate, console state).
Host-update operator action while recovering: run Invoke-HostUpdate.ps1 -Release with the request id to end the update.
Host-update operator action: read the remarks and reason the state file lists.
Host-update refusal reason: the private root's filesystem does not qualify for the single-flight locks.
Host-update refusal reason: the account's home directory could not be verified.
Host-update failure reason: the step child's runtime directory is not the one the request names.
Host-update failure reason: the host identity file is missing or empty; a step never mints one.
Host-update refusal reason: a one-shot run holds the host. Action end_one_shot.
Host-update refusal reason: a VM is kept for diagnosis. Action release_diagnostic_hold.
Host-update refusal reason: the runner is to be started and its sudo rule is missing. Action provision_elevation.
Host-update refusal reason: the runner's launch record cannot be read, so the runner could not be started the same way.
Host-update refusal reason: another request holds the runner gate.
Host-update failure reason: a runner process could not be identified safely, so nothing was stopped.
Host-update failure reason: a runner process was still alive when the stop phase ended.
Host-update failure reason: the source update did not complete.
Host-update failure reason: the checkout is not at the commit the request expected.
Host-update reason: the checkout's host-update protocol differs from the controller's, and no new snapshot could be staged; an expired request carries it.
Host-update refusal reason: the request expired before a controller claimed it.
Host-update failure reason: the runner start failed for a reason no other code names.
Host-update failure reason: the started runner did not acknowledge readiness in time.
Host-update failure reason: the started runner exited before acknowledging readiness.
Host-update failure reason: the console multiplexer answered in a way that leaves its session state unknown. Action act_at_host.
Host-update failure reason: a step child ended without a usable result three times.
Host-update remark: the runner started without a console (no multiplexer, a socket path too long, or no session created).
Host-update remark: the pull kept a held framework ring.
Host-update remark: the checkout is on a detached HEAD.
Host-update remark: the runner runs with NoGitPull, so the source update was skipped.
Host-update remark: the status service is disabled for this runner, so the listener phase was skipped.
Runner console of a host update on KVM: the runner runs in a tmux session on the controller's socket.
Host-update capability and route reason: no host controller holds its lock on this host.
Host-update capability reason: the controller's state says its session cannot start a runner.
Host-update capability, route and verdict reason: the controller does not run the scope asked for.
Host-update route refusal: the caller is not this host by the loopback rule.
Busy holder kind: a host update holds the host; the reply names its id and the host-update state URL.
Host-update phase 3: stop the runner's processes.
Host-update phase 4: update the checkout.
Host-update phase 8: start the status listener; also the debt action of an armed listener obligation.
